exposure: Gestational weight gain (categorized as adequate, excessive, low, stable, or weight loss)
outcome: Admission to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU)
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 29,408 pregnant individuals with obesity experiencing singleton livebirths in Northern California between 2008 and 2013.
finding: Weight loss during pregnancy was associated with an increased risk of small-for-gestational age infants across all obesity classes, but not with other adverse perinatal outcomes, and it potentially reduced the risk of cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: Weight loss during pregnancy was associated with a decreased risk of cesarean delivery among individuals with obesity class III.
